name: REJOICE
question: Do vaginal estradiol soft-gel inserts improve dyspareunia and vaginal atrophy measures compared with placebo in postmenopausal women?

design.population: Postmenopausal women aged 40–75 years with moderate-to-severe dyspareunia as their most bothersome symptom, vaginal pH above 5.0, and at most 5% superficial vaginal cells.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized superiority trial
design.locator: Methods, Study design and Study participants; Results, Participant disposition

verdictNote: All doses met all four coprimary endpoints at week 12.
takeaway: In REJOICE, vaginal estradiol soft-gel inserts at 4, 10, or 25 µg improved dyspareunia, vaginal cytology, and pH versus placebo at 12 weeks in postmenopausal women with symptomatic vulvar and vaginal atrophy.

reports.label: Sexual-function analysis
reports.citation: Kingsberg SA, Derogatis L, Simon JA, et al. "TX-004HR Improves Sexual Function as Measured by the Female Sexual Function Index in Postmenopausal Women With Vulvar and Vaginal Atrophy: The REJOICE Trial." *J Sex Med.* 2016;13(12):1930-1937. doi:10.1016/j.jsxm.2016.09.002
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Methods, Study Design, p 1931

results.measure: Least-squares mean change from baseline to week 12 in total Female Sexual Function Index score; observed baseline and week-12 means and denominators

values.e4: LS mean change +7.91; observed 14.8 (n=173) to 22.6 (n=153); not significantly different from placebo
values.e10: LS mean change +9.43; observed 15.8 (n=170) to 24.8 (n=154); versus placebo P < 0.05
values.e25: LS mean change +10.28; observed 14.2 (n=172) to 24.8 (n=156); versus placebo P = 0.0019

results.note: FSFI was a secondary endpoint analyzed by ANCOVA with baseline as covariate in the modified intention-to-treat population; the paper reports no between-arm confidence intervals.
results.locator: Full text, Statistical Analyses, p 1932; Table 2, p 1933; Figure 1 and Discussion, p 1934

results.measure: Observed baseline to week-12 domain mean scores, with assessment denominators; between-arm change comparisons by ANCOVA

values.e10: Pain 1.8 (n=170) to 4.3 (n=154); lubrication 2.2 (n=170) to 4.4 (n=154); each versus placebo P ≤ 0.015
values.e25: Pain 1.7 (n=172) to 4.2 (n=156); lubrication 2.0 (n=172) to 4.3 (n=156); each versus placebo P ≤ 0.015

results.note: Only the 10 and 25 µg doses differed from placebo for pain and lubrication; no between-arm confidence intervals were reported.
results.locator: Full text, Results, Sexual Function, p 1932; Table 2, p 1933; Figure 2, p 1935

results.measure: Observed baseline to week-12 domain mean scores, with assessment denominators; between-arm change comparisons by ANCOVA

values.e25: Arousal 2.7 (n=172) to 4.1 (n=157), P = 0.0085 versus placebo; satisfaction 2.9 (n=172) to 4.6 (n=157), P = 0.0073 versus placebo

results.note: Only 25 µg differed from placebo for arousal and satisfaction. Desire and orgasm did not differ from placebo at any dose; no between-arm confidence intervals were reported.
results.locator: Full text, Results, Sexual Function, p 1932; Table 2, p 1933; Figure 2, p 1935

harms.label: Study discontinuation owing to adverse events
harms.note: 1.8% of women overall; event count and arm-specific counts not reported in this secondary analysis.
